RoomType.rationale: OwlMagistrateNormal declares RoomType.Monster. The sim has no room_type field on Encounter itself; instead run.py picks the encounter FROM the bucket matching the map node's room type (normal_keys -> RoomType.MONSTER), so bucket membership is the sim's counterpart. owl_magistrate sits only in normal_keys, never in weak/elite/boss_keys -- correct.

AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: C# declares the single-element superset [OwlMagistrate], identical to what GenerateMonsters always returns -- this encounter has no variable composition. The sim has no dedicated per-encounter AllPossibleMonsters property (its only cross-encounter monster vocabulary is full_env.py's global _monster_classes(), which enumerates every Monster subclass in the game, not a per-encounter superset); for a FIXED-composition encounter like this one Encounter.monster_classes is exactly equivalent, since nothing else could ever spawn here, so there is no possible divergence to find.

GenerateMonsters.rationale: C#: one monster, no slot tag (the tuple's string half is null), zero RNG draws. Sim: one monster class, monster_slots left at its default empty tuple so the seated monster's slot_name stays None (matches null), and create_monsters just does `cls(hooks, rng) for cls in monster_classes` with no draw of its own for composition. Roster, order (trivial, one element) and draw count (0) all match.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.maps_to: the Encounter dataclass (sts2_rl/monsters/base.py) is never registered as a hook listener; only Monster instances register themselves in Monster.__init__
ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false says the encounter object itself never joins the hook walk. The sim's Encounter is a plain dataclass with no hook methods and is never passed to HookSystem.register anywhere in combat.py/cmds.py -- only the Monster objects it produces register. Structurally the same fact, trivially true on both sides.

guards.what: MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward -- not overridden by OwlMagistrateNormal, so it inherits EncounterModel's RoomType ladder (Monster: 10-20) x AscensionHelper.PovertyAscensionGoldMultiplier under Poverty
guards.rationale: sts2_rl/rewards.py GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER] = (10, 20), and the OWL_MAGISTRATE_NORMAL Encounter passes neither min_gold nor max_gold, so roll_gold_reward falls back to that range -- matches the base ladder exactly. The Poverty ascension multiplier is not modelled (rewards.py's own module docstring: 'non-ascension values only (no Scarcity/Poverty scaling)'); ascension values are out of scope per audit/tools/PROMPT.md's Scope section, so this is not filed as a gap.

guards.what: ShouldGiveRewards / IsWeak -- neither overridden by OwlMagistrateNormal, both default (true / false)
guards.rationale: Encounter.should_give_rewards defaults to True (sts2_rl/monsters/base.py) and OWL_MAGISTRATE_NORMAL does not set it. owl_magistrate is listed only in _glory_rooms().normal_keys, never in weak_keys -- consistent with IsWeak's inherited false.
